I farm cotton on my 10.1 mu every year. Forty years I have been doing this, so I know my land well. Just the two of us at home now — my wife helps me, the children work in town.

For seed, I buy the improved Bt cotton seed from the dealer in town. The old varieties get eaten by bollworm — I learned that the hard way in the 90s. Bt seed costs more but saves on spraying. Neighbors all use it too.

Land preparation — I plough deep before planting, then level it. Cotton needs loose soil for the taproot. I plant in late April when the soil is warm enough.

Fertilizer is my biggest cost so I think carefully. Last year I used about 2 bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu as base, that is 50 kg, plus one bag of urea (50 kg) as topdressing at flowering. That gives me about 18 kg nitrogen, 7-8 kg phosphorus, 7-8 kg potassium per mu. I will do the same — why change what works? Cotton needs potassium for boll filling, so I will not skip it.

Water — I have the well, so I irrigate 3 times: once before planting to wet the soil, once at bud stage, once at peak flowering. If July is very dry I add a fourth. Cotton does not like too much water though, the roots rot.

Pesticide — even with Bt, I still spray for aphids, spider mites, plant bugs. Usually 5-6 sprays through the season. Bt handles bollworm but not the other pests. I watch the field every few days.

Expected yield — good year I get 250 kg seed cotton per mu, bad year 200. I aim for 240.
